channel.title: Bellevue Dispatch
channel.description: Bellevue news, once a week, from the Bellevue Dispatch.

item.title: The budget now carries a 0.1% transportation sales tax
item.description: On Nov. 3, council voted 5–1 for a hybrid option that uses the Transportation Benefit District for a 0.1%, 10-year sales tax, with no car-tab fee increase.

item.title: $15 million is set aside to move Fire Station 6
item.description: Council unanimously designated $15 million in long-range planning reserves to buy land for a new site for the aging station.

item.title: Free naturalist training opens for the Class of 2027
item.description: Classes run Jan. 26 to April 29, Tuesday and Thursday evenings 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., with some Saturday field trips.

item.title: BEACON, the city's equity and outreach advisory network, is adding members
item.description: It advises the city on making programs and services easier to reach.

item.title: get ready for the first windstorm
item.description: Windstorm season is the time to set this up, before the lights go out.

item.title: Why the fire-damaged building on 100th Avenue NE near NE 1st Street is still standing, and whether anything is planned
item.description: A reader in Downtown asked why the fire-damaged building on 100th Avenue NE near NE 1st Street is still standing, and whether anything is planned.

item.title: The final budget hearing drew nearly 40 speakers
item.description: Council closed the public hearing on the 2027–2028 operating budget and the 2027–2032 capital plan on Tuesday, October 27, with 63 written comments on file.

item.title: 146 apartments on 118th Avenue SE got design approval
item.description: The October 28 permit bulletin lists a decision of approval with conditions for a seven-story apartment building at 995 118th Avenue SE, on the site of a partly built hotel in West Bellevue.

item.title: A community open house on the Diversity Advantage Plan 2035 is Nov. 19
item.description: The city will showcase progress on the plan at a community open house, Thursday, Nov. 19, 6 to 8 p.m., at City Hall, 450 110th Avenue NE. Source

item.title: clear the storm drains by the curb
item.description: Fall leaves can block the storm drains next to your curb.

item.title: Where tradespeople and service trucks will park as high-rise housing fills in
item.description: A reader in Downtown asked where tradespeople and service trucks will park as high-rise housing fills in.

item.title: Both rezones passed; parking comes back for a final vote
item.description: On October 20, council approved the EverGlen Village and Bellewood Townhomes rezones.

item.title: The budget's last public hearing
item.description: The final hearing on the 2027–2028 budget was on Tuesday's agenda, with adoption expected in November.

item.title: What Bellevue will ask Olympia for
item.description: The draft 2027 state agenda opposes changes to the business and occupation tax that would cut into local B&O, backs the I-405 Renton to Bellevue project, and asks for $280,000 for a kitchen at Highland Community Center.

item.title: Ballots are due Tuesday
item.description: Election Day is November 3, and drop boxes close at 8 p.m.

item.title: A seat on the Human Services Commission is open
item.description: The commission advises council on human services planning and funding.

item.title: drain the hoses before the first freeze
item.description: Bellevue Utilities asks owners to protect their own pipes.

item.title: Where the aquatic center planned for Bellevue Airfield Park stands
item.description: A reader in Eastgate asked where the aquatic center planned for Bellevue Airfield Park stands.

item.title: Permits would cost more in 2027
item.description: Staff brought the proposed development fees to Tuesday's budget session.

item.title: Parking minimums are shrinking, and council picks how far
item.description: State law requires Bellevue to cut many minimum parking requirements by January 27, 2027.

item.title: Last week's votes
item.description: Council adopted the children and family services sales tax on October 13, effective January 1.

item.title: Eastrail's last southern gap is in for permits
item.description: King County applied to build 1.7 miles across I-90, reusing the steel bridge over 14 freeway lanes and the wooden trestle over 32nd Street.

item.title: Help pick the backyard cottage plans
item.description: The city will offer up to 10 pre-approved designs for backyard cottages and cottage homes, at a set price.

item.title: test the alarms when the clocks change
item.description: Clocks fall back Sunday, November 1.

item.title: Your water, sewer and storm bill would rise 8.5% next year and 8.6% in 2028
item.description: Those are the rates the city's Environmental Services Commission recommended, and staff presented them at Tuesday's budget session.

item.title: The transportation tax district moves onto council's own agenda, with no tax attached yet
item.description: Council voted 6–1 on October 6 to take over the Transportation Benefit District directly, and the ordinance was on Tuesday's consent calendar.

item.title: A county sales tax starts in January. The question is whether Bellevue keeps its share
item.description: King County passed a 0.01% tax for children and family services on October 6, one cent on $100.

item.title: One Planning Commission seat is open
item.description: It is a four-year volunteer term for a Bellevue resident, with meetings on the second and fourth Wednesdays at 6:30 p.m.

item.title: The parks plan is being rewritten
item.description: The Parks and Open Space System Plan guides land purchases, trails and future park levies.

item.title: rake out the storm drain before the rain does
item.description: Bellevue has more than 20,000 storm drains, and in October, leaves are what block them.

item.title: Council has the ten-year street list, and a sales tax and car-tab fee could pay for more of it
item.description: At Tuesday's budget session, staff laid out three scenarios for 2027–2036 transportation projects.

item.title: Fourteen speed cameras by year-end
item.description: Council has authorized 14 cameras, and the city says all of them will be in place by the end of 2026.

item.title: Bellevue residents aged 15 to 24 can get up to $5,000 for a climate project
item.description: Teams of at least two people apply, the work has to happen in Bellevue, and it has to be finished by March 30, 2027.

item.title: The Network on Aging has open seats
item.description: Members serve three-year terms and give 6 to 12 hours a month.

item.title: The 2 Line has a new stop
item.description: Pinehurst Station, at 130th Street and 5th Avenue NE in North Seattle, opened September 30, five years ahead of its original schedule.

item.title: know the tree rules before the windstorms
item.description: In Bellevue, a significant tree is at least 6 inches across, measured 4.5 feet above the ground, and a landmark tree is at least 24 inches.

item.title: The budget math, in one number: about sixteen dollars
item.description: Council spent September 22 on the revenue side of the preliminary 2027–2028 budget and the 2027–2032 capital plan.

item.title: The Spring District's north blocks would become housing instead of offices
item.description: Wright Runstad has applied to amend the Spring District master plan: the blocks north of the light rail line switch from office to residential and residential-with-retail, with below-grade parking, a realigned roadway and a new linear park.

item.title: Bellevue is planning its largest reservoir
item.description: The Meydenbauer South Reservoir is meant to carry growth and firefighting capacity across western Bellevue.

item.title: Four crosswalks got painted, and the city is asking whether they work
item.description: Nikita Ares and Kenji Stoll designed two each: 164th Avenue NE at NE 24th Street, 124th Avenue NE at NE 8th Street, 132nd Avenue NE at Bel-Red Road, and 106th Avenue NE at NE 10th Street.
